items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons were masters of that style.

ctx.x: Had you done boogie-woogie before? That’s like Albert Ammons and that stuff.

Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons were masters of that style. By the way, his son, Gene Ammons, was a fine saxophonist. I did some recording with him. But, yeah, that style was very popular at that particular time in the 40s. It was in the late 40s or early 50s. I did a lot of it, I wasn't too thrilled about it, but I did a lot of it. I didn't think I did that well.
